svg.aria-label: Fig 1. The planned Arthai Health flow. All nine steps are planned and none is built. A claim goes from the claim builder to the payer mock, remit posting and the triage step with the CCI gate. If the gate is sure, the claim goes to the appeal writer. If not, it goes to a human in the review console. After tier 2 human approval of the appeal, the voice agent calls only the payer mock. AR follow-up reads claim status from the payer mock. Reviewer edits go to eval and then back to the gate.
svg.title: Fig 1. The planned Arthai Health flow. All nine steps are planned and none is built. A claim goes from the claim builder to the payer mock, remit posting and the triage step with the CCI gate. If the gate is sure, the claim goes to the appeal writer. If not, it goes to a human in the review console. After tier 2 human approval of the appeal, the voice agent calls only the payer mock. AR follow-up reads claim status from the payer mock. svg.text: Synthetic data only. Design from PR #9 / #14 research, not yet decided. None is built.
1 Claim builder and scrubber: builds the 837 claim file and runs the NCCI and MUE edits.
2 Payer and clearinghouse mock: our own fake payer. It sends 835 and 277 files.
3 Remit posting: reads the 835 remittance and finds each denied line.
4 Triage + CCI gate: the triage step (LLM by default, LAYA optional) and the CCI gate pick the path.
5 Review console + audit: the human queue, the approvals and the audit trail.
6 Appeal writer: an LLM drafts the letter (Muse planned, D-011 proposed). Each statement cites a source.
7 Voice agent: a browser call to the mock payer rep.
8 AR follow-up: reads the 276/277 claim status and ranks the open claims for the next action.
9 Eval and feedback loop: reviewer edits become eval cases.
black: the claim goes to the next step (1 to 2 to 3 to 4, then 6 to 7).
green: the gate is sure. The claim goes from 4 to 6.
red: the gate is not sure. The claim goes from 4 to the human queue in 5.
amber: the claim goes from the human queue in 5 to the writer in 6.
Step 6 includes the citation gate and the tier 2 approval in the console (Fig 3).
In the hackathon, 6 to 7 starts only after that human approval.
grey: the 276/277 claim status goes from the payer mock in 2 to AR follow-up in 8.
dashed: the call goes only to our mock payer in 2.
blue dotted: reviewer edits go from 5 to 9, then recalibrate the gate in 4.
Fig 4 shows how the call outcome goes back to the console.
